You write small, pure-Python helpers for a bot that plays a GUESSING game (the bot tries to find a hidden secret using feedback after each guess). Read the rules and the sample observation, then write these module-level functions:

candidate_space(variant) -> iterable of hashable secrets: every value the secret can take = every legal guess. `variant` is a dict; variant["rules"] holds the rules text (parse the ranges/lengths from it with `re`).
extract_history(observation) -> list of (guess, feedback) for OUR OWN guesses so far, oldest first, exactly as the observation text reports them (ignore the opponent's guesses at our secret). `guess` must be a member of candidate_space; `feedback` any hashable value (e.g. the word or a tuple of counts).
feedback(secret, guess) -> the feedback the game would give for `guess` if the hidden secret were `secret`; the SAME form and values extract_history returns, so that feedback(true_secret, g) == the feedback printed in the observation.
format_guess(guess) -> the action string to send, exactly in the rules' action format (one line).
max_guesses(variant) -> int, the rules' limit on how many guesses we get (None if unlimited).

RULES:
GUESS THE NUMBER - range 1-100, at most 12 guesses each.

SETUP
The arena gives each player a secret whole number between 1 and 100 (inclusive), chosen at
random. You know your own number; your opponent is trying to find it. You are trying to find
your opponent's number. (The two numbers are independent and may even be equal.)

TURN ORDER
Player 0 guesses first, then Player 1, alternating. One "round" = one guess by each player.

ACTION FORMAT
    guess <n>
where <n> is a whole number from 1 to 100 (digits only). Examples:  "guess 50"   "guess 1"   "100"
(a bare number also works). Numbers outside the range or any other text are illegal
(first time: a warning and the same turn again; second time: you lose the game). Repeating an
earlier guess is legal but wastes a turn.

FEEDBACK
After each guess you are told about the OPPONENT's secret number:
    "higher"  : their number is greater than your guess
    "lower"   : their number is smaller than your guess
    "correct" : you found it
You also see every guess your opponent made at YOUR number and the feedback they got.

WHAT YOU OBSERVE
Your own secret number, the round, all your guesses with feedback and all the opponent's guesses
with feedback. Example line:  "Round 2: you guessed 50 -> higher (their number is above 50)".

HOW THE GAME ENDS AND IS SCORED
The game is checked at the END of every round, so both players always get the same number of guesses:
- if only one player has found the opponent's number, that player wins;
- if both found it in the same round, it is a draw.
Guess cap: after round 12, if nobody has found it, the player whose feedback narrows the opponent's
number down to FEWER possible values wins (e.g. "between 40 and 44" = 5 values beats "between 10 and
29" = 20 values); equal = draw. Score: winner 1, loser 0, draw 0.5 each.

GUESS THE NUMBER - range 1-100, at most 12 guesses each.

SETUP
The arena gives each player a secret whole number between 1 and 100 (inclusive), chosen at
random. You know your own number; your opponent is trying to find it. You are trying to find

TURN ORDER
Player 0 guesses first, then Player 1, alternating. One "round" = one guess by each player.

ACTION FORMAT

FEEDBACK
After each guess you are told about the OPPONENT's secret number:

    "correct" : you found it

WHAT YOU OBSERVE

HOW THE GAME ENDS AND IS SCORED
The game is checked at the END of every round, so both players always get the same number of guesses:
- if only one player has found the opponent's number, that player wins;
- if both found it in the same round, it is a draw.
